question: What is the chemical name of Plaster of Paris?
solution:
The correct answer is __Calcium Sulphate Hemihydrate.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**Plaster of Paris/Calcium Sulphate Hemihydrate (CaSO4·1/2H2O):

__
 
• It is a white powdery substance that is commonly used in the medical field for casting broken bones.
 
• It is created by heating gypsum, a mineral found in sedimentary rocks.
 
• When mixed with water, it forms a paste that hardens quickly and is used in construction for creating molds and sculptures.
 
• It is also used in the food industry as a coagulant for tofu and as a calcium supplement in certain types of bread.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• **Calcium Acetate (Ca(C₂H₃O₂)₂**:

 
 
• It is a calcium salt used in medical treatments to control phosphate levels in patients with kidney disease.
 
• In its chemical form, it can also act as a food preservative and is used in various industrial applications.
 
 
 
• **Calcium Sulphate Dihydrate(CaSO₄·2H₂O):**
 
 
• It is a hydrated form of calcium sulfate, commonly known as gypsum, used in the construction industry to make plaster and drywall.
 
• It is also used in the food industry as a firming agent, particularly in tofu production, and as a coagulant.
 
 
 
• Calcium carbonate (CaCO3):
 
 
• Similar to the minerals calcite and aragonite, it is a common component found in rocks, particularly in chalk and limestone, eggshells, gastropod shells, shellfish skeletons, and pearls.
 
• It is the primary component of agricultural lime and is created when carbonate ions and calcium ions in hard water combine to form limescale.
 
• It has medical use as a calcium supplement or as an antacid.
